heading: Best Brunch in Penticton
title: Best Brunch & Breakfast in Penticton | Okanagan Roam
description: Where to brunch in Penticton: a beachfront Turkish brunch, lakeside patios, big diner breakfasts, vegan and gluten-free spots, bakeries and good coffee.
intro: Penticton does weekend mornings well. You can book a Turkish brunch on the beach, eat eggs Benny on a lakeside patio, order a breakfast poutine at a diner the hotel concierges recommend, or carry coffee and cake across the road to the grass beside Okanagan Lake.
These are the brunch and breakfast spots worth knowing, grouped by the kind of morning you're after.

items.name: Bench Market
items.text: a popular cafeteria-style breakfast, brunch and market spot, and a handy pitstop on a Naramata Bench wine tour. The gluten-free options are excellent, and dogs are welcome on the outdoor terrace.

items.name: Mack's Social House
items.text: a dog-friendly restaurant with a swing indoors. The $3 Sunday mimosas are poured with visible generosity, and the Pavé potatoes are good enough to order on their own.

items.name: Creperie Ooolala Bistro
items.text: regulars say it feels like a trip to Paris. The room is tiny, the staff speak French and the atmosphere isn't put on for tourists. Let the staff guide your order.

items.name: Creperie Ooolala - Food truck
items.text: the original food truck behind the bistro, where French staff turn out traditional buckwheat crêpes that taste straight out of Brittany.

sections.jump: With a view or a patio
sections.heading: With a view or a patio

items.name: Elma
items.text: a beachfront Turkish restaurant with an exceptional weekend brunch. Book ahead, and come back another night for the charcoal octopus.

items.name: Palmer Kitchen + Spirits
items.text: a hotel restaurant worth visiting on purpose, with a lake view and a patio. The duck confit Benny is surprisingly good, and the room stays quiet and unhurried.

items.name: Bufflehead Café
items.text: the breakfast spot inside Penticton Lakeside Resort, with a lakeside patio. The eggs Benny are the standout and the Starbucks coffee refills are free. The patio can run short on shade, so bring sun protection.

items.name: MATCH Eatery & Public House
items.text: weekend brunch inside Cascades Casino Penticton, with a rooftop patio, backyard games and valley views.

items.name: All Roads Cafe
items.text: order a coffee and a slice of housemade cake, then walk it across the road to lawn seating right on Okanagan Lake.

items.name: Terry's Comfort Food
items.text: a classic, no-frills diner on Main St with enormous breakfast portions like the King Omelette. Kids love the free jellybean machine.

items.name: Bear's Den Restaurant
items.text: a reliable diner that local hotel concierges recommend, with generous portions and friendly service. The specialties are the Bear Meal and the Hunter's Surprise breakfast poutine.

items.name: Tootsies Diner
items.text: a cool, vintage locals' favourite in the industrial park. Classic oldies play, there's a retro record table, and the pancakes are fluffy.

items.name: Shades on Main Restaurant
items.text: a family-style breakfast spot with large private booths. Order the onion rings for the dill sauce reviewers mention most.

items.name: Stillfood Bistro & Cappuccino Bar
items.text: a fully vegan brunch bistro confident enough to win over skeptics. Celiac guests can trust the gluten-free options too.

items.name: MAKU
items.text: a gluten-free-friendly sushi burrito spot with vegan options and a dog-friendly patio. Bring the dog along.

items.name: Marmalade Bakery
items.text: a from-scratch cake shop run by sisters Kyra and Caelin, inside Skaha Pizza in the Yorkton Plaza, with dedicated vegan and gluten-free lines. Drop in for daily baked goods, grab-and-go lunch and specialty coffee. It was voted Best Cake Shop in the 2026 Best of Penticton.

items.name: One14 Coffee Co.
items.text: small-batch roasted coffee inside a converted industrial complex. Reviewers call the gluten-free oat cookie good in its own right, not a token dietary option.

items.name: Petrasek Bakery
items.text: a charming artisan bakery and café on Main St that feels like stepping into Paris. Order fresh bread or pastries, and expect the owners to know you by name after a visit or two.

items.name: South Main Market
items.text: a family-run neighbourhood grocery with a from-scratch bakery at its heart. Locals line up for the cinnamon buns, and it was voted Best Bakery in the 2026 Best of Penticton. Grab a sandwich on house-made buns for an easy beach lunch.

items.name: Wayne & Freda
items.text: a bustling café attached to a mercantile shop, with a patio where dogs are welcome. It's right by the farmers market.

items.name: Atomic Coffee House
items.text: a stylish Main St coffee shop with cool decor and a jazz soundtrack. The Nanaimo bar is pleasantly not too sweet.

items.name: soe cafe
items.text: an eclectic spot filled with pottery and built around music, with vinyl for sale. Order the matcha.
